question: What's a good solar generator with panels for home backup?
query: best solar generators for home backup 2026 EcoFlow Anker SOLIX BLUETTI battery capacity solar panels comparison

replays.text:
**My pick for most homes: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus**—it has a 3.84 kWh battery, 6,000 W output and 120/240 V power, so it’s a stronger fit for home backup than a small camping-style power station. It accepts up to 3,200 W of solar input and can be expanded with extra batteries. ([Specs and comparison](https://ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/best-solar-generators-for-home-backup))

One catch: the results don’t confirm that solar panels are included with the F3800 Plus. Check for a panel bundle, or buy compatible panels separately; the guide lists two solar inputs rated up to 1,600 W each. For powering hardwired home circuits, plan on a transfer switch or home panel installed by an electrician—don’t connect it through a dryer outlet. ([Backup setup guidance](https://ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/best-solar-generators-for-home-backup))

If you want a larger, expandable system for longer outages, the [EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra](https://us.ecoflow.com/products/delta-pro-ultra?variant=40758830071881) scales up to 90 kWh and provides 120/240 V output; its solar-panel bundle details should also be checked before buying.

For a strong home-backup setup, I’d look at the **Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus**: it has a 3.84 kWh battery, 6,000 W output, 120/240 V support for larger loads such as a well pump, and up to 3,200 W of solar input. It’s also expandable if you later need more runtime. ([Specs and comparison](https://ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/best-solar-generators-for-home-backup))

Pair it with compatible solar panels, but **check whether the price you’re considering includes panels**—the source lists the generator’s solar-input capacity, not a panel bundle. For a more expandable whole-home system, the [EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra](https://us.ecoflow.com/products/delta-pro-ultra?variant=40758830071881) supports 120/240 V and can scale up to 90 kWh; its page also doesn’t make clear that panels are included.

For hardwired home circuits, plan on a properly installed transfer switch or home power panel—don’t plug a generator into a household outlet. ([Backup setup guidance](https://ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/best-solar-generators-for-home-backup))

For **home backup, I’d look at the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus** if you need to run bigger loads or 240V equipment such as a well pump. It has a 3.84 kWh battery, 6,000 W output, and up to 3,200 W of solar input; it can also be expanded with extra batteries. [See the F3800 Plus comparison and specs](https://ecosolarkits.com/blogs/guides/best-solar-generators-for-home-backup).

If you mainly want backup for essentials—like a fridge, lights, and electronics—the **EcoFlow DELTA Pro** is another good option: it starts at 3.6 kWh and can expand to 25 kWh. EcoFlow describes solar charging and home-backup configurations, including a transfer-switch setup. [See the DELTA Pro](https://us.ecoflow.com/products/delta-pro-portable-power-station?hl=en-US).

**One thing to check before buying:** panels may be sold separately, and the right number depends on how quickly you want to recharge. To power home circuits, plan on a proper transfer switch or home panel installed by an electrician—don’t plug a generator into a household outlet.
